00831.urgent: 04 / action language Know when to call Emergency: call 112/999 Collapse, severe bleeding or vomiting blood, severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, seizure, sudden new vision loss or a major neurological change. Tell responders you receive atezolizumab and bevacizumab. Contact oncology urgently Black stools, any concerning bleeding, severe or persistent diarrhoea, new cough or breathlessness, yellow eyes, reduced urine, new severe headache, new vision changes, marked weakness, confusion, a temperature ≥37.5°C or ≤36°C, or feeling suddenly unwell. Follow your centre’s SOS instructions even if a symptom begins after the last cycle. Medicines and fever Measure your temperature before paracetamol or ibuprofen if you feel unwell, and contact your team for advice. Do not self-start steroids for suspected immune toxicity. Ask before using anti-inflammatory painkillers, herbal products or new medicines, particularly if you have liver disease or bleeding risk. What about anti-sickness or a PPI? The NCCP lists both medicines as having minimal emetogenic potential and says premedication is not usually required. No routine antiemetic or PPI script is invented here. Continue medicines actually prescribed to you and ask for a reconciled list if you are unsure.
00831.version: Advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma / NCCP 00831 v2a

00831.indication: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab for advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma where appropriate.
